purpose: Screen BFAR Region II's CY 2021 Annual Report for independent inland-fish source leads in Quirino and Batanes, while separating catch retrieval, stocking, and landing-site counts from wild occurrence evidence.

source.title: CY 2021 Annual Report
source.provider: Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, Regional Office II
source.reviewedPages: Printed pages 2, 24-25; PDF index text for inland-resource, landing-site, BASIL stocking, and IAS retrieval sections.
source.license: No item-specific reuse license was identified in the reviewed report pages.

reviewedEvidence.nagtipunanRetrieval: The report says BFAR Region II and local partners identified janitor fish and flower horn as invasive alien species in the Cagayan River Basin, with collection areas listed by province/municipality. It reports 52 kg of janitor fish retrieved from Enrile, Cagayan (50 kg) and Nagtipunan, Quirino (2 kg). It does not name the Nagtipunan waterbody, sampling/collection date, collector, specimen ID, or exact fish taxon for the 2 kg.
reviewedEvidence.nearbyScientificLabel: The same section describes a proposed CSU study on janitor fish skin and prints the name 'Pterygoplichtys pardalis'. The report does not explicitly crosswalk that proposal's label to the fish retrieved in Nagtipunan; preserve the typo as source text and do not assign the species to the 2 kg catch without a specimen-level link.
reviewedEvidence.stockingIsNotOccurrence: The BASIL section says eels/elvers and ayungin were stocked in the Cagayan River, while tilapia fingerlings were stocked in a previous BASIL management-area small water impounding project. No exact stocking station, event date, fish species identification for ayungin, or release-to-monitoring crosswalk is provided in the reviewed pages. Stocked fish do not establish a naturally occurring population.
reviewedEvidence.batanesCoverage: The report lists 75 NSAP landing sites (73 marine and two freshwater) and separately lists 23 landing sites in Batanes, but does not identify which Batanes sites are freshwater or tie any freshwater site to a fish checklist. The province-level count cannot be treated as inland-water coverage.
reviewedEvidence.regionalSiteQueue: The report describes Magat Dam/Reservoir, Cagayan River, 174 small water impounding projects, and 25 diversion dams as regional inland resources, but does not provide a complete per-waterbody fish inventory. Its printed landing-site breakdown (75 total versus listed counts of 23 Batanes, 49 Cagayan, 9 Isabela, and two Cagayan River Basin) does not reconcile arithmetically and the categories are not explained in the reviewed section.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The Nagtipunan entry is a municipal-level purchased/retrieved IAS total, not a standardized survey event or a named river/lake occurrence.
The report's proposed Pterygoplichtys pardalis label is not linked to the Nagtipunan catch; do not resolve the catch to species from the adjacent paragraph.
BASIL fish releases, aquaculture production, and inland-water infrastructure are context only and must not be used as evidence of wild distribution or native status.
The landing-site counts are internally inconsistent or differently scoped in the reviewed text; no Batanes freshwater presence or absence can be inferred from them.
No fish occurrence rows, coordinates, geometry, current legal/safety claims, or app content can be derived from these passages. No item-specific reuse terms were verified.
nextAction: Trace the Nagtipunan 2 kg retrieval to its named waterbody, collection date, photograph, sample record, and verified scientific identity. Search independent Batanes inland-water surveys or specimen-backed records; do not assume marine landing-site coverage represents freshwater fauna. Use the BFAR inland-resource list only as a site-discovery queue.
